jobs.title: Product Manager, Link Growth [Consumer]
jobs.descriptionHtml:
We believe that the way people interact with their finances will drastically improve in the next few years. We’re dedicated to empowering this transformation by building the tools and experiences that thousands of developers use to create their own products. Plaid powers the tools millions of people rely on to live a healthier financial life. We work with thousands of companies like Venmo, SoFi, several of the Fortune 500, and many of the largest banks to make it easy for people to connect their financial accounts to the apps and services they want to use. Plaid’s network covers 12,000 financial institutions across the US, Canada, UK and Europe. Founded in 2013, the company is headquartered in San Francisco with offices in New York, Seattle, Washington D.C., Raleigh, London, and Amsterdam.

Plaid’s Consumer team owns all of Plaid’s consumer facing surfaces. This includes Link, Plaid’s flagship product, which has been used by over half of all US adults to share their information safely and securely with financial applications. Link drives the vast majority of Plaid’s revenue. We’re also building out Plaid’s first B2C product, which is an exciting, 0-1 space for us. Both areas are top business priorities.

Responsibilities

As the Link Growth PM, you will own conversion at Plaid and evolve it for a growingly agentic world. Link is the front door to Plaid’s products, so this is a meaningfully large responsibility: (1) Any improvement in Link conversion has direct revenue impact, and (2) We’re seeing a massive uptick in AI-companies launching fintech products, so making Link compatible for their use cases is one of our highest priorities.

You will define the roadmap for the above and partner with cross-functional team to hit your goals:
• Drive prioritization and execution (build, measure, iterate)
• Identify opportunities through consumer feedback and staying close to our data / dashboards
• Partner with cross-functional team (design, research, data science, ML, legal, and compliance) to do all of the above

Qualifications

  • 5+ years in product management, building consumer onboarding, growth, or related products, shipping consumer-facing changes

  • You have successfully launched consumer facing features through rapid experimentation driving meaningful outcomes in the user journey and represented via metrics

  • You can communicate complex concepts succinctly for broad audiences to drive decisions

  • You have driven roadmap and prioritization exercises and shown that you have driven clear impact through your decisions

Other things that matter

  • You thrive in a culture of high ownership, velocity, and throughput, and speak your mind regardless of level

  • You have a strong opinion on both UX and data

We're looking for a Creative Producer to manage the end-to-end production of creative work across Plaid's marketing and brand campaigns, from paid ad content and growth marketing assets, to event activations, to partner and customer marketing deliverables. This role partners closely with marketing, brand, and design to keep creative work moving: intake is clear, timelines are realistic, quality bars are met, and nothing falls through the cracks between "we need this" and "it's shipped." You thrive on variety. One week you might be managing production for a paid digital campaign, the next coordinating creative for an on-site event activation.

This is an execution-focused role: you take defined project plans and briefs and run them with rigor, using sound judgment on day-to-day production decisions while partnering with your manager/stakeholders on more ambiguous or higher-stakes calls.

Responsibilities

  • Manage production for paid marketing campaigns, coordinating asset creation, timelines, and approvals across creative and marketing stakeholders

  • Support partner and customer marketing projects, producing creative deliverables that meet both brand standards and partner/customer requirements

  • Own creative production logistics for some of our events, including coordinating signage, activations, sponsorship assets, and on-site creative needs

  • Own and support the creative request intake process, ensuring requests come in with clear briefs, are triaged appropriately, and routed to the right owner

  • Run polish reviews on outgoing creative to catch quality, consistency, and brand issues before assets ship

  • Build and maintain production timelines across multiple concurrent projects, coordinating vendors and freelancers as needed and flagging risks or budget issues early

  • Communicate status, blockers, and changes clearly to creative and marketing stakeholders

Qualifications

  • 3-5 years of experience in creative production, project coordination, or production management, agency or in-house, across marketing/brand campaigns

  • Experience producing across multiple creative formats (paid media, event/experiential, digital, print, or similar)

  • Highly organized, with strong attention to detail and comfort managing several concurrent projects with different stakeholders and timelines

  • Clear, proactive communicator who can coordinate across creative, marketing, and external vendors without dropping details

  • Working familiarity with project tracking tools (e.g., Linear, Monday.com, Asana, or similar) and comfort ramping into new ones

  • Comfortable executing against plans and priorities, while exercising independent judgment on day-to-day production decisions

  • Growth mindset: curious about new formats and channels, and willing to adapt as the work evolves

jobs.descriptionHtml:
We believe that the way people interact with their finances will drastically improve in the next few years. Plaid powers the tools millions of people rely on to live a healthier financial life. Plaid’s network covers 12,000 financial institutions across the US, Canada, UK and Europe. Founded in 2013, the company is headquartered in San Francisco with offices in New York, Seattle, Washington D.C., Raleigh, London, and Amsterdam.

Plaid’s Corporate Finance team leads company-wide financial planning, forecasting, and reporting, delivering strategic insights to internal and external stakeholders. We align financial goals with business objectives to support informed decision-making at the senior leadership and executive levels.

What excites us:

  • 3+ years of relevant FP&A experience, ideally in Corporate Finance, G&A support, or a broader FP&A role.

  • An “act like an owner” mindset: you take initiative, follow through on commitments, and ask for guidance when needed. You’re eager to learn and take on more responsibility.

  • A solid foundation in core FP&A activities, including month-end close, reporting, variance analysis, and forecasting, with exposure to annual planning and a working knowledge of accounting principles.

  • Strong analytical skills and experience building or maintaining financial models. You care about accuracy and enjoy understanding the business drivers behind the numbers.

  • Clear communication and a collaborative approach, with the ability to explain findings, ask thoughtful questions, and build relationships with business partners.

  • Curiosity about AI, automation, and process improvements, with an interest in developing systems skills. Familiarity with Pigment, Adaptive, Anaplan, or similar FP&A tools is a plus.

What excites you:

  • You enjoy a fast-paced, high-growth environment where you can learn quickly and gain experience across multiple areas.

  • You’re energized by stretching beyond your day-to-day responsibilities, being scrappy, and taking on new challenges that help you learn and grow.

  • You like improving how work gets done, whether that means simplifying a process, automating a recurring task, or making an analysis more useful.

  • You enjoy digging into the numbers, understanding business drivers, and turning your findings into clear insights that help inform decisions.

  • You value working closely with Finance, Accounting, and business teams, building relationships and learning from their perspectives.

  • You’re excited to develop your systems skills in Pigment, our FP&A platform, and partner with our systems lead to build models, dashboards, and workflows.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
We believe that the way people interact with their finances will drastically improve in the next few years. We’re dedicated to empowering this transformation by building the tools and experiences that thousands of developers use to create their own products. Plaid powers the tools millions of people rely on to live a healthier financial life. Plaid’s network covers 12,000 financial institutions across the US, Canada, UK and Europe. Founded in 2013, the company is headquartered in San Francisco with offices in New York, Seattle, Washington D.C., Raleigh, London, and Amsterdam.


Team Overview

Plaid's TechOps team is the technical foundation that is a major stakeholder in keeping the company running. We own the systems, tools, and infrastructure that every Plaid employee depends on from identity and endpoint management to help desk support, office infrastructure, and the internal tooling that powers day-to-day productivity.

What sets us apart from a traditional IT team is how we approach the higher level goals we have to improve our systems and tooling over time. We treat corporate infrastructure like an engineering problem: configuration lives in code when possible, endpoint provisioning is automated, access assignment is self-service, and we're always looking for ways to make our systems more reliable and our support burden smaller. We've built real momentum in that direction, and we're investing in the people and tools to take it further.

We're a small team with broad ownership and high standards. We work closely with Security, Engineering, and People teams to make sure Plaid's internal environment is secure, scalable, and ready for where the company is going whether that's a new office, a new compliance requirement, or a new way of working enabled by AI tooling.

Role Overview

While you would be required to take part in our on-call rotation for a few hours a week, this isn't just a break/fix IT position, it's a chance to build, improve and own systems that a thousand-person company depends on.

If you care about doing IT the right way, infrastructure as code, automation-first, and are very security-minded, this team is actively building that culture and we need someone with existing experience in this area to help us move even faster.

In this role you will be expected to own various domains, extend existing capability for the team on a longer term roadmap and work on larger scope (quarter or longer) and more complex projects.

Responsibilities

  • Leading others on the team, unblocking others and providing some guidance and mentorship.

  • Helping the team build out its roadmap, advocating for work that should be done in the future and backing it up with a plan.

  • Owning and improving Okta configuration, lifecycle policies, access reviews, MFA enforcement, Workflows automation

  • Managing endpoint configuration via Iru/Kandji, with a preference for policy-as-code and version-controlled configs

  • Building and maintaining automation to reduce repetitive support burden

  • Evaluating, deploying and supporting AI tooling to improve team and company productivity

  • SaaS procurement/renewals for the systems we own

  • Active ownership of many companywide SaaS platforms (Google Workspace, Linear, Slack, Okta etc.)

  • Supporting other Eng, Security and GTM teams with planned work that crosses into the team boundary of the systems we support or our expertise.

  • 3 days a week in the office

Qualifications

  • Must have experience:

    • 5+ years of experience supporting a large fleet of macOS devices

    • mobile device management for Apple devices (Iru, Intune, Workspace One etc.)

    • configuration as code (ex: terraform)

    • Advanced usage of bash/python or other languages

    • leveraging Claude Code, Codex or other tools to improve the quality and efficiency of the solutions you are building

  • Experience managing, but also defining and leading the business with the proper use of critical central business systems

    • Google Workspace

    • Slack

    • Linear/Jira or other ticketing platforms

To support that mission, we seek to build a diverse team of driven individuals who care deeply about making the financial ecosystem more equitable. jobs.title: Senior Financial Analyst, Corporate Finance & Strategy
jobs.descriptionHtml:
We believe that the way people interact with their finances will drastically improve in the next few years. We’re dedicated to empowering this transformation by building the tools and experiences that thousands of developers use to create their own products. Plaid powers the tools millions of people rely on to live a healthier financial life. We work with thousands of companies like Venmo, SoFi, several of the Fortune 500, and many of the largest banks to make it easy for people to connect their financial accounts to the apps and services they want to use. Plaid’s network covers 12,000 financial institutions across the US, Canada, UK and Europe. Founded in 2013, the company is headquartered in San Francisco with offices in New York, Seattle, Washington D.C., Raleigh, London, and Amsterdam.

We are looking for a Senior Financial Analyst to join the Corporate Finance team. This is the strategic, externally-oriented arm of the team — covering the board process, long range planning, capital structure, SBC and equity modeling, and enterprise-level financial strategy. You will partner closely with the CFO, Leadership, the Board, Corp Dev, and Accounting on the decisions that shape Plaid’s long-term financial trajectory.

 

What excites us:

  • 5+ years of work experience including financial planning & analysis, corporate finance, investment banking, private equity, strategic finance, or management consulting — ideally with tech, SaaS, or fintech exposure.

  • Advanced financial modeling skills, with hands-on experience building long range, scenario/sensitivity, or valuation models.

  • Strong command of consolidated financial statements, key SaaS / fintech operating metrics, and external benchmarking.

  • Excellent communication and storytelling skills — able to move fluidly between granular model detail and an executive-level narrative for senior leaders and the Board.

  • Proven ability to partner cross-functionally and distill complex, ambiguous topics into structured frameworks and clear recommendations.

  • Proactive self-starter with intellectual curiosity, a can-do attitude, and the ability to thrive in a high-autonomy, fast-paced environment.

  • Passion for leveraging AI, automation, and systems thinking to drive operational excellence, improve financial processes, and build scalable planning and decision report frameworks.

 

What excites you:

  • Own components of Plaid’s 3–5 year long range plan — model design, scenario analysis, and translation of company strategy into financial targets.

  • Partner on end-to-end PMO of the quarterly Board process, including framework development, narrative ownership, materials build, and Q&A management.

  • Build and operationalize SBC and equity modeling, incorporating HC growth, grant cadence, forfeitures, and refresh cycles — and tie SBC into the path to GAAP profitability, EBITDA, and margin analysis.

  • Lead consolidated cash flow forecasting and contingency / management reserve strategy, and run total company forecast reviews against company targets.

  • Drive external benchmarking against peer companies on key financial and non-financial metrics, and build the analytical foundations that inform long-term capital and operating decisions.

  • Partner with Corp Dev on capital raise activities, including pro-forma reporting, forecasting, and capital structure analysis.

  • Perform ad hoc analyses that influence long-term business planning and decision-making.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
We believe that the way people interact with their finances will drastically improve in the next few years. Plaid powers the tools millions of people rely on to live a healthier financial life. Plaid’s network covers 12,000 financial institutions across the US, Canada, UK and Europe. Founded in 2013, the company is headquartered in San Francisco with offices in New York, Seattle, Washington D.C., Raleigh, London, and Amsterdam.

Our EPD Recruiting team builds the teams that build Plaid. We partner with leaders across Engineering, Product, Design, Data, and Security to deliver thoughtful, candidate-first recruiting experiences that raise the bar for how we scale.

We are responsible for delivering world-class technical talent through pragmatic, data-informed, and principle-aligned recruiting practices. We believe the hardest hires are won upstream, in the research and the reach-out, long before a loop is ever scheduled. Our mission is to help Plaid grow intentionally by hiring exceptional people who share our values and drive our mission to unlock financial freedom for everyone.

We are hiring a Technical Sourcer to build the pipelines for Plaid’s core Engineering and Data Science population. You will own the top of the funnel across one or multiple tech pipelines, from market research and pipeline strategy through to qualified candidates entering the interview process.

You will carry a high req load across multiple teams at once, and you will do it without losing the details that make a pipeline trustworthy. You will also turn what you learn into intelligence the team can use: where the talent actually sits, what competitors are building and paying for, and what a role needs to look like to be winnable.

The quality of what enters our funnel shapes every hiring decision downstream.

Responsibilities:

  • Own top-of-funnel strategy and execution for technical reqs across Software Engineering or Data Science. You build the pipeline, engage and qualify the candidate, and hand off a qualified, well-briefed person to the recruiter.

  • Run talent research. Market maps, org mapping, open-source and technical community research, and advanced boolean and x-ray search across sources most people do not think to check.

  • Write outreach that gets answered. You personalize based on what someone has actually built, you test your messaging, and you own your response rate as a number you can explain.

  • Operate at volume without losing precision. You run multiple searches at once with disciplined follow-up cadences, accurate ATS hygiene, and clean data that others can trust.

  • Turn research into intelligence. Build market maps, talent density views, and competitive hiring insights, then bring them to recruiters and hiring managers to shape role scope, leveling, and search strategy.

  • Build diverse pipelines by design, through the breadth of your research and the inclusivity of your outreach, not as a screening step at the end.

  • Partner closely with recruiters and hiring managers on calibration. You bring the market back into the room when a role as written is not findable, and you propose what would make it winnable.

  • Track and report your funnel. Response rate, screen pass rate, and stage conversion tell you where to spend your next hour. Use them, and share what they say.

  • Represent Plaid authentically. You are often a candidate's first impression of us, and that first conversation sets the tone for everything after it.

Qualifications:

  • 3+ years of technical sourcing experience, including in-house sourcing at a high-growth technology company.

  • Strong sourcing research technique and tooling: boolean and x-ray search, LinkedIn Recruiter, GitHub and technical communities, publications and conference sources, and CRM or ATS sourcing workflows. You can find people who are not searchable by just title or company name.

  • Demonstrated success in high-volume, high-urgency environments, carrying multiple technical searches at once without dropping the details.

  • Genuine fluency in technical skill sets. You can read a job spec, a GitHub profile, or a research paper and make a defensible call on relevance.

  • Strong written and verbal communication. Your outreach is short, specific, and human, and senior engineers reply to it.

  • Data discipline. You use funnel metrics to decide where to spend effort, and you can explain your pipeline with numbers rather than anecdotes.

  • Meticulous attention to detail and personal ownership of your data hygiene. If your pipeline data is wrong, no one downstream can plan.

  • A candidate-first approach built on empathy, transparency, and consistent follow-through.


Nice-to-Have:

  • Experience sourcing in fintech, financial services, or another regulated environment.

  • Experience producing talent intelligence or market mapping work that was presented to senior leadership and changed a hiring decision.

  • Experience building sourcing playbooks or evaluating and rolling out sourcing tooling.

  • Experience sourcing for distributed teams.

  • Familiarity with inclusive sourcing practices and a track record of building diverse technical pipelines.

Responsibilities

  • Act as a trusted advisor to hiring managers, providing data, market insights, and feedback to guide decision-making.

  • Lead debriefs and manage closing strategies that align with Plaid’s hiring bar and candidate experience standards.

  • Track and analyze recruiting metrics to identify bottlenecks and continuously improve efficiency and quality.

  • Collaborate with sourcers, coordinators, and cross-functional partners to ensure a seamless and consistent recruiting experience.

  • Represent Plaid’s culture and mission authentically throughout the recruiting process.

Qualifications

  • 5 to 8 years of full-cycle recruiting experience, including experience hiring Product Managers.

  • Deep understanding of product management disciplines, including strategy, execution, and technical fluency.

  • Strong sourcing capability with experience identifying and engaging top PM talent in competitive markets.

  • Proven success partnering with senior product leaders to shape hiring decisions and influence outcomes.

  • Skilled closer with experience negotiating offers and managing candidate relationships through final stages.

  • Data-driven mindset; comfortable using recruiting metrics and market insights to inform decisions.

  • Candidate-first approach with a focus on empathy, transparency, and thoughtful communication.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience partnering strategically with C-suite and senior executives, providing counsel on talent strategy and market insights.

  • Experience in a client lead or embedded recruiting model (acting as a strategic partner to product teams).

  • Exposure to high-growth SaaS or fintech recruiting environments.

  • Experience building recruiting playbooks or process improvements for Product hiring.

  • Familiarity with inclusive hiring practices and strategies for building diverse product teams.

jobs.title: Senior Security Analyst, Security Risk Management
jobs.descriptionHtml:
We believe that the way people interact with their finances will drastically improve in the next few years. We’re dedicated to empowering this transformation by building the tools and experiences that thousands of developers use to create their own products. Plaid powers the tools millions of people rely on to live a healthier financial life. We work with thousands of companies like Venmo, SoFi, several of the Fortune 500, and many of the largest banks to make it easy for people to connect their financial accounts to the apps and services they want to use. Plaid’s network covers 12,000 financial institutions across the US, Canada, UK and Europe. Founded in 2013, the company is headquartered in San Francisco with offices in New York, Seattle, Washington D.C., Raleigh, London, and Amsterdam.

About the team:

The Security Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) team is part of Plaid’s security organization, focused on enabling the business by proactively managing information security risks and maintaining effective controls.

Our mission is to reduce the likelihood and impact of security risks while operating a robust assurance program that builds trust with our customers, consumers, and data partners.We partner closely across the company to ensure Plaid’s platform remains secure, resilient, and aligned with industry and regulatory expectations.Security risk management is how Plaid makes informed security trade-offs—we identify and analyze the risks that could materially affect the business, make sure the right owners decide what to do about them, and turn that picture into reporting leadership and the board can act on.

About the role:

  • You will run security risk assessments end-to-end within Plaid’s security risk management program—intake, scenario-based analysis, treatment decisions, and monitoring across security, infrastructure, and product risk.

  • You will work with engineering SMEs and risk owners on risks ranging from over-privileged access and supply-chain gaps to product abuse and AI adoption, giving owners a clear, defensible basis for accepting or mitigating each one.

  • You will build quarterly security risk reporting and the security risk content in leadership and board materials.

  • You will help integrate security risk into enterprise risk management, so it is tracked and weighed alongside the rest of the business.

  • You will help mature the program as its scope grows, and operate as an AI power user who automates the work so it scales.

Responsibilities:

  • Run Security Risk Assessments: Triage intake, run scenario-based risk analyses with engineering SMEs, score initial and residual risk, and drive risk owners to a documented treatment decision. Your analysis turns vague concerns into decisions leadership can stand behind.

  • Build Quarterly Risk Reporting: Gather updates on material risks, prepare the Security Risk Review, and build the security risk content for executive and board decks. Your reporting gives leadership a clear, current view of where security risk sits and what’s being done about it.

  • Integrate Security Risk into ERM: Partner with enterprise risk stakeholders to map security risks into the enterprise taxonomy, align rating scales, and keep the registers in sync. Your work puts security risk alongside business risk instead of in a silo.

  • Mature the Program: Help evolve the risk framework, register, key risk indicators, and risk-owner self-service as the program’s scope grows. Your work moves the program from tracking risks to measuring and reducing them.

  • Support FedRAMP 20x Risk Decisions: Help make sure unmet FedRAMP rules and KSI gaps carry a documented risk explanation and senior-official acceptance in the Security Decision Record, consistent with the risk register. Your work keeps Plaid’s FedRAMP risk posture defensible to agencies and assessors.

  • Scale Through AI and Automation: Build AI skills and automations for intake triage, first-draft risk analyses, register hygiene, and report generation—and share them across the team. Your approach lets the program cover more risk without adding headcount.

Qualifications:

Must haves:

  • Security risk assessment:

    • Experience running scenario-based analyses of technical risks (cloud, IAM, software supply chain, application and product) using NIST SP 800-30, FAIR, or a comparable method.

    • Technical depth to engage engineers on architecture and controls, and to tell a real exposure from a hypothetical one.

  • Risk program maturity and ERM integration:

    • Experience building or maturing a security risk program—methodology, register, treatment and exception workflow, and key risk indicators.

    • Experience integrating security risk into an enterprise risk management program.

  • Risk reporting and executive communication:

    • Experience preparing quarterly risk reporting and building security risk content for executive and board decks.

    • Ability to turn technical risk into a concise executive narrative without overstating or hand-waving.

  • Security and compliance knowledge:

    • Working knowledge of NIST 800-53, NIST CSF, ISO 27001, and SOC 2, and how risk management feeds each.

  • AI fluency and tooling:

    • Power user who has built AI skills, agents, or automations that materially increase risk-program throughput—and who shares what works with the team.

Nice to have:

  • Hands-on FedRAMP 20x experience, including Security Decision Record reporting for rules and Key Security Indicators (SDR-CSO-FRR, SDR-CSX-KSI).

 - You will help integrate security risk into enterprise risk management, so it is tracked and weighed alongside the rest of the business.

 - You will help mature the program as its scope grows, and operate as an AI power user who automates the work so it scales.


RESPONSIBILITIES:

 - Run Security Risk Assessments: Triage intake, run scenario-based risk analyses with engineering SMEs, score initial and residual risk, and drive risk owners to a documented treatment decision. Your analysis turns vague concerns into decisions leadership can stand behind.

 - Build Quarterly Risk Reporting: Gather updates on material risks, prepare the Security Risk Review, and build the security risk content for executive and board decks. Your reporting gives leadership a clear, current view of where security risk sits and what’s being done about it.

 - Integrate Security Risk into ERM: Partner with enterprise risk stakeholders to map security risks into the enterprise taxonomy, align rating scales, and keep the registers in sync. Your work puts security risk alongside business risk instead of in a silo.

 - Risk program maturity and ERM integration:
   
   - Experience building or maturing a security risk program—methodology, register, treatment and exception workflow, and key risk indicators.
   
   - Experience integrating security risk into an enterprise risk management program.

 - Risk reporting and executive communication:
   
   - Experience preparing quarterly risk reporting and building security risk content for executive and board decks.
   
   - Ability to turn technical risk into a concise executive narrative without overstating or hand-waving.

   - Working knowledge of NIST 800-53, NIST CSF, ISO 27001, and SOC 2, and how risk management feeds each.

jobs.title: Staff Product Manager - Data Supply Expansion
jobs.descriptionHtml:
We believe that the way people interact with their finances will drastically improve in the next few years. We’re dedicated to empowering this transformation by building the tools and experiences that thousands of developers use to create their own products. Plaid powers the tools millions of people rely on to live a healthier financial life. We work with thousands of companies like Venmo, SoFi, several of the Fortune 500, and many of the largest banks to make it easy for people to connect their financial accounts to the apps and services they want to use. Plaid’s network covers 12,000 financial institutions across the US, Canada, UK and Europe. Founded in 2013, the company is headquartered in San Francisco with offices in New York, Seattle, Washington D.C., Raleigh, London, and Amsterdam.

About the Team
Our Connectivity team’s mission is to unlock the potential of the Plaid network by broadening and deepening our connection to data partners. We do this by providing solutions that allow our data partners to be part of the network and by providing best in class connections. By expanding and improving our connections to data providers, we are able to strengthen the Plaid network while also enabling great products and experiences.

About the role:

You will decide what data Plaid goes after next. Bank data got us here, but the picture our customers need now includes things we do not have: property tax, merchant and SKU-level purchases, utilities, tax, payroll. Some of it we should build with our own technology. Some of it we should partner or pay for. Someone has to make those calls with conviction and a real business case behind them, and that person is you.

This is a 0-1 role. You will start with two to three engineers and a mandate to prove something real: Plaid's first non-bank data offering, live, inside your first year. Along the way you will set the multi-year strategy for supply expansion, define what quality and completeness mean for data types nobody here has worked with before, and build the internal case that turns a promising vertical into a funded bet.

Responsibilities:

  • Set the multi-year strategy for non-bank data supply, grounded in what our products and customers need rather than what is technically interesting

  • Build and quickly execute against the one year plan - showcasing fast momentum and impact

  • Force-rank new data types across the company and own the business case for each, including the ones you recommend against

  • Make and defend build, buy, and partner decisions alongside data partnerships, corporate development, and legal

  • Ship Plaid's first non-bank data offerings, as internal insight inputs or externalized to customers

  • Partner with engineering and data teams on the taxonomies, quality controls, and coverage metrics that new data types require

  • Define the metrics for supply expansion and report progress to leadership and cross-functional stakeholders

Qualifications:

  • 8+ years of experience, including 5+ in product management or equivalent founder/operator roles.

  • Analytical rigor: You are comfortable working directly with data, cost models, and operational metrics to make and defend complex decisions.

  • Deep technical fluency: You can reason about large-scale systems, load management, API platforms, and machine-learning models and engage engineers as a close product partner.

  • Platform & systems thinking mindset: You think in systems, and design for reuse and the long term.

  • Leadership, stakeholder influence, and communication :You should be comfortable working cross-functionally (engineering, data, product) and influencing without direct authority. You must be able to explain complex technical ideas to non-technical stakeholders, drive alignment, and make trade-offs crystal clear

  • Have a founder mentality: you’ve gotten something off the ground before, whether a company, net new product, or new vertical market and navigated the headwinds to do it

jobs.title: Commercial Lead, Banking and Wealth
jobs.descriptionHtml:
We believe that the way people interact with their finances will drastically improve in the next few years. We’re dedicated to empowering this transformation by building the tools and experiences that thousands of developers use to create their own products. Plaid powers the tools millions of people rely on to live a healthier financial life. We work with thousands of companies like Venmo, SoFi, several of the Fortune 500, and many of the largest banks to make it easy for people to connect their financial accounts to the apps and services they want to use. Plaid’s network covers 12,000 financial institutions across the US, Canada, UK and Europe. Founded in 2013, the company is headquartered in San Francisco with offices in New York, Seattle, Washington D.C., Raleigh, London, and Amsterdam.


The go-to-market teams at Plaid combine deep market, technical, and product knowledge to help customers obtain Plaid services to build and scale amazing applications. Plaid is looking for an experienced professional to facilitate our commercial relationships with some of the largest names in fintech and financial services. The right candidate has honed business instincts and can drive strong commercial outcomes that position our customers and Plaid for success.

You will serve as a thought partner, contract expert, and at times, lead negotiator for major deals. Your work is thoroughly impactful as you will define the commercial terms that underpin the relationships between Plaid and its customers. You're motivated by tangible outcomes and finding win-win deals to strike with customers.

You'll also be a key partner to the broader set of Plaid’s go-to-market teams. You will help craft repeatable, robust commercial processes for an increasingly global team, leading to more speed and consistency. You enjoy rolling up your sleeves and diving into data analysis to make more educated decisions. You're keen on transparency and visibility to enable sharper decision-making and organizational communication.

Responsibilities

  • Collaborate closely with Plaid’s Sales, Account Management, and Banking and Wealth teams to negotiate key customer contracts

  • Creatively enable new deals with top prospects while staying true to Plaid’s operating practices

  • Drive successful renewals, upsells, and cross-sells with top customers to increase usage and adoption of key Plaid products

  • Craft pricing strategies that work for Plaid, prospects, and existing customers

  • Evolve and improve commercial terms, practices, and processes

  • Serve as the GTM expert on a given GBT with regard to commercialization, pricing, and agreement requirements for new products and services

  • Serve as the GTM voice and single point of contact for cross-functional special projects

Qualifications

  • 4-7 years of experience in strategic sales, business development, finance/consulting, partnerships or GTM strategy—ideally with customer-facing ownership of complex, high-value commercial agreements.

  • Proven track record of negotiating complex deals, including multi-product or multi-party agreements in regulated industries such as financial services or fintech.

  • Demonstrated success working cross-functionally with Product, Legal, Engineering, and GTM teams to shape deals, align priorities, and unblock high-stakes internal initiatives.

  • Strong executive communication skills to confidently engage senior external stakeholders.

  • Experience building scalable commercial frameworks (e.g., pricing strategies, decision processes) that support speed and consistency across a growing GTM org.

  • Deep interest in fintech, open finance, and technical products, with the ability to understand and advocate for product capabilities in commercial conversations.

  • Comfort with ambiguity and change, with a bias for action and a growth mindset suited to fast-paced, high-growth environments.

jobs.title: Product Manager, Privacy & Data Governance
jobs.descriptionHtml:
We believe that the way people interact with their finances will drastically improve in the next few years. We’re dedicated to empowering this transformation by building the tools and experiences that thousands of developers use to create their own products. Plaid powers the tools millions of people rely on to live a healthier financial life. We work with thousands of companies like Venmo, SoFi, several of the Fortune 500, and many of the largest banks to make it easy for people to connect their financial accounts to the apps and services they want to use. Plaid’s network covers 12,000 financial institutions across the US, Canada, UK and Europe. Founded in 2013, the company is headquartered in San Francisco with offices in New York, Seattle, Washington D.C., Raleigh, London, and Amsterdam.

Data Governance builds the infrastructure that ensures Plaid responsibly manages sensitive consumer financial data. This includes identifying and managing PII (including deletions), enforcing consent and other data use limitations, upholding data minimization, and anonymizing data, while unblocking velocity for internal teams.

Responsibilities

  • Own the product strategy and execution for privacy, data governance, and responsible data use across Plaid’s platform

  • Ensure Plaid’s products and internal systems handle consumer data in ways that are compliant, transparent, secure, and aligned with Plaid’s values and commitments

  • Serve as the connective PM between Legal, Security, Data, Engineering, and Product teams to operationalize privacy requirements into scalable product solutions

  • Define and drive the roadmap for privacy-related platform capabilities (e.g., consent, data minimization, retention, deletion, access controls)

  • Translate evolving regulatory requirements into clear product requirements and system designs

  • Partner with Legal, Policy, and GTM to proactively identify privacy risks and opportunities in new and existing products

  • Work closely with Engineering to design privacy-by-default and privacy-by-design architectures

  • Balance strong privacy protections with usability and performance for customers and developers

Qualifications

  • 3+ years of product management or equivalent experience in a B2B environment

  • Ability to influence and collaborate with cross-functional partners in Legal, Engineering, Policy, and Compliance to balance risk with product innovation

  • Strong communication skills, both written and verbal; able to simplify complex concepts for diverse audiences

  • Experience working on platform, infrastructure, or highly regulated products

Nice to Have

  • Experience with design and implementation of privacy initiatives to deliver best-in-class privacy practices,

  • Experience with data protection domains such as data lifecycle management, access control, or automated policy enforcement.

  • Experience in fintech or API-driven B2B products

  • Experience in data management, observability, or quality

Plaid powers the tools millions of people rely on to live a healthier financial life. We work with thousands of companies like Venmo, SoFi, several of the Fortune 500, and many of the largest banks to make it easy for people to connect their financial accounts to the apps and services they want to use. Plaid’s network covers 12,000 financial institutions across the US, Canada, UK and Europe. Founded in 2013, the company is headquartered in San Francisco with offices in New York, Seattle, Washington D.C., Raleigh, London, and Amsterdam.

As a Product Manager on the AI & Data Foundations team, you will build the shared platforms that power Plaid’s AI and data capabilities. This is early-stage, hands-on work: you’ll partner with data, ML, and platform engineers to take capabilities from 0→1 and scale them into infrastructure that is accessible, reliable, and easy to use across Plaid. Your scope will span our AI platform (e.g., LLM gateway, eval infrastructure), our data platform (e.g., Databricks, AI-powered data tooling), and the systems connecting the two.


This role is for an experienced platform PM who is excited about the rapidly evolving intersection of data infrastructure and AI. You are technically fluent, strategic, and execution-oriented, and know how to turn emerging capabilities into reliable platforms, primitives, and tools that other teams can build on.

 

Responsibilities

  • AI & Data Foundations Strategy: Define the vision, roadmap, and success metrics for the shared platforms that power data and AI development across Plaid.

  • Platform Development: Partner with data, ML, and platform engineers to design and ship foundational capabilities spanning AI infrastructure, developer tooling, data platforms, pipelines, quality, and governance.

  • Internal Developer Experience & Adoption: Build platforms that Plaid teams choose to use. Develop a deep understanding of internal users, remove friction from common workflows, and measure success through adoption, developer velocity, reliability, and quality.

  • Platform Evolution: Balance immediate needs from product teams with longer-term platform investments, identifying where Plaid should standardize, build shared primitives, enable experimentation, and/or leverage an existing external solution.

  • Cross-Functional Leadership: Partner with product, engineering, data, research, and security to identify shared needs and embed foundational AI and data capabilities across Plaid.

  • Communication & Alignment: Translate complex technical decisions and platform trade-offs into clear narratives that enable decisions across technical and non-technical stakeholders.

 

Qualifications

  • 8+ years of product management experience including direct experience building AI/ML platform systems, applied intelligence products, or other data infrastructure from concept to production

  • Deep technical fluency in modern data and AI/ML systems, including how data is stored and processed and how models are developed, evaluated, deployed, and monitored. You can engage deeply with engineers and data scientists on architecture and technical trade-offs without needing to be the engineer in the room.

  • Demonstrated success operating in ambiguous, early-stage environments, turning loosely defined problems into decisions, shipped capabilities, and measurable adoption or impact.

  • Ability to operate in a fast-paced startup environment

  • Platform mindset and experience building scalable developer or data platforms through well-designed primitives, APIs, and frameworks.

  • Strategic and executional range. Skilled at setting the long-term vision while also delivering near-term experiments, specs, prototypes, and launches.

  • Strong communicator and cross-functional leader who can translate complex technical concepts into clear narratives to drive decisions for technical and non-technical stakeholders.

  • Commitment to responsible AI and transparency, especially in regulated or high-trust domains.

  • [Nice to Have] Hands-on experience with LLMs, embeddings, or agentic systems in production.

  • [Nice to Have] Experience building AI developer tooling in production.

  • [Nice to Have] Familiarity with applied AI in regulated or high-trust domains such as fintech, identity, or risk.

 

Our mission at Plaid is to unlock financial freedom for everyone. To support that mission, we seek to build a diverse team of driven individuals who care deeply about making the financial ecosystem more equitable. We recognize that strong qualifications can come from both prior work experiences and lived experiences. We encourage you to apply to a role even if your experience doesn't fully match the job description. We are always looking for team members that will bring something unique to Plaid!

Plaid is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and values diversity at our company. We do not discriminate based on race, color, national origin, ethnicity, religion or religious belief, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, transgender status, sexual stereotypes, age, military or veteran status, disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. We also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state, and local laws. Plaid is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for candidates with disabilities in our recruiting process. If you need any assistance with your application or interviews due to a disability, please let us know at accommodations@plaid.com.

jobs.title: Model Governance Lead, Credit
jobs.descriptionHtml:
We believe that the way people interact with their finances will drastically improve in the next few years. We’re dedicated to empowering this transformation by building the tools and experiences that thousands of developers use to create their own products. Plaid powers the tools millions of people rely on to live a healthier financial life. We work with thousands of companies like Venmo, SoFi, several of the Fortune 500, and many of the largest banks to make it easy for people to connect their financial accounts to the apps and services they want to use. Plaid’s network covers 12,000 financial institutions across the US, Canada, UK and Europe. Founded in 2013, the company is headquartered in San Francisco with offices in New York, Seattle, Washington D.C., Raleigh, London, and Amsterdam.

About the Team

We drive the evolution of Model Governance for Plaid’s Credit products. We work closely with Plaid’s Credit insights team, including Product, Data Science, and Engineering, to support the development and responsible use of next-generation Credit scores and attributes based on cash flow and Plaid’s network.


About the Role

As the Model Governance Lead, Credit, you will own and execute the Model Governance program for Plaid’s Credit products. You will help ensure that the models supporting Plaid’s Credit Score and Insights products are conceptually sound, appropriately validated, well-documented, and fit for their intended use.

You will work independently while partnering closely with model owners and cross-functional stakeholders. You will provide thoughtful challenge, identify risks and limitations, and help teams improve models and governance practices over time.


What Excites You

  • Building and evolving a model risk governance framework for an important Credit product portfolio.

  • Independently assessing the conceptual soundness, data, features, performance, stability, and intended use of credit models.

  • Identifying model weaknesses and translating them into clear, actionable remediation plans.

  • Partnering with Product, Data Science, and Engineering teams to strengthen model development and validation practices.

  • Creating clear, rigorous documentation that helps customers understand and trust the models behind Plaid’s Credit products.

  • Bringing curiosity, sound judgment, and constructive challenge to complex modeling decisions.

  • Helping shape responsible use of machine learning as Plaid develops new Credit scores and attributes.


What Excites Us

  • 7+ years of experience building and owning a model governance program.

  • Experience in model validation, model risk management, model development, or Data Science.

  • Deep knowledge of models built for credit purposes.

  • Strong understanding of machine learning modeling concepts and techniques, such as XGBoost, and what constitutes rigorous, defensible model validation.

  • Familiarity with newer modeling techniques, such as foundation models and neural networks.

  • Experience assessing data and feature inputs, conceptual soundness, model performance, stability, limitations, and appropriateness of use.

  • A genuinely independent, detail-oriented, and curious mindset.

  • Comfort providing meaningful challenge to model owners and stakeholders rather than simply documenting their work.

  • Experience working at a FinTech is a plus.

jobs.title: Product Manager - Data Supply Health and Traffic
jobs.descriptionHtml:
We believe that the way people interact with their finances will drastically improve in the next few years. We’re dedicated to empowering this transformation by building the tools and experiences that thousands of developers use to create their own products. Plaid powers the tools millions of people rely on to live a healthier financial life. We work with thousands of companies like Venmo, SoFi, several of the Fortune 500, and many of the largest banks to make it easy for people to connect their financial accounts to the apps and services they want to use. Plaid’s network covers 12,000 financial institutions across the US, Canada, UK and Europe. Founded in 2013, the company is headquartered in San Francisco with offices in New York, Seattle, Washington D.C., Raleigh, London, and Amsterdam.

About the Team
Our Network Enablement and Access team works to unlock the potential of Plaid's network by broadening and deepening our connections with data partners. We build the capabilities that help data providers participate in the network, strengthen the quality and reliability of those connections, and enable great products and experiences for Plaid's customers.

Within Network Enablement and Access, the Data Supply Traffic and Health team owns how Plaid's requests flow to the data providers we depend on. We manage the load placed on each provider, the constraints that shape our access, and the fair allocation of capacity across Plaid's products and new initiatives. As paid access expands across the network, we also work to keep that traffic reliable, efficient, and cost-effective.

 

As the Product Manager for Data Supply Health and Traffic, you will establish and lead a new product area at the foundation of every Plaid product. You will define how Plaid allocates constrained provider capacity, scales traffic across products, and manages the economics of paid data access.

 

You will also optimize for data freshness, balancing timeliness with provider capacity and cost so Plaid's products can deliver better experiences to end users. You will own the strategy and roadmap, partner closely with engineering and data-provider teams, and turn technical, contractual, and commercial constraints into clear product priorities.

 

This is a highly analytical and cross-functional role for someone who enjoys creating structure where no established playbook exists. In your first year, you will build the operating framework for traffic allocation and fairness, develop a clear view of paid-access cost and efficiency, and establish the metrics Plaid uses to run and improve this area.

 

Responsibilities:

  • Define and own Plaid's strategy and roadmap for data-supply traffic, health, and cost efficiency.

  • Build and prioritize traffic-optimization initiatives, including opportunities created by evolving machine-learning models and strategic concessions negotiated with providers.

  • Serve as the bridge between Plaid's data-provider relationship teams and internal product teams, translating provider constraints into internal priorities and product demand into clear asks of providers.

  • Partner deeply with engineering and data teams to understand system behavior, evaluate technical trade-offs, and turn analysis into decisions.

  • Establish and track the core traffic and cost metrics needed to operate the area, identify risks, and measure progress.

     

Qualifications:

  • 8+ years of experience, including 5+ in product management or equivalent founder/operator roles.

  • Analytical rigor: You are comfortable working directly with data, cost models, and operational metrics to make and defend complex decisions.

  • Deep technical fluency: You can reason about large-scale systems, load management, API platforms, and machine-learning models and engage engineers as a close product partner.

  • Platform & systems thinking mindset: You think in systems, and design for reuse and the long term.

  • Leadership, stakeholder influence, and communication :You should be comfortable working cross-functionally (engineering, data, product) and influencing without direct authority. You must be able to explain complex technical ideas to non-technical stakeholders, drive alignment, and make trade-offs crystal clear.

Our mission at Plaid is to unlock financial freedom for everyone. To support that mission, we seek to build a diverse team of driven individuals who care deeply about making the financial ecosystem more equitable. We recognize that strong qualifications can come from both prior work experiences and lived experiences. We encourage you to apply to a role even if your experience doesn't fully match the job description. We are always looking for team members that will bring something unique to Plaid!

Plaid is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and values diversity at our company. jobs.title: Technical Support Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
We believe that the way people interact with their finances will drastically improve in the next few years. We’re dedicated to empowering this transformation by building the tools and experiences that thousands of developers use to create their own products. Plaid powers the tools millions of people rely on to live a healthier financial life. We work with thousands of companies like Venmo, SoFi, several of the Fortune 500, and many of the largest banks to make it easy for people to connect their financial accounts to the apps and services they want to use. Plaid’s network covers 12,000 financial institutions across the US, Canada, UK and Europe. Founded in 2013, the company is headquartered in San Francisco with offices in New York, Seattle, Washington D.C., Raleigh, London, and Amsterdam.

This position requires employees to be primarily located within the Pacific Time Zone and to work Pacific Time business hours.

Plaid Support ensures our customers' applications can help their consumers live their best financial lives by ensuring our products continue to operate as expected. We investigate the root cause of integration issues, quantify their scope and impact, and when we can’t fix them ourselves, we work with our Growth and Engineering teams to reach a solution.  

 

As we continue to grow, we’re looking for Technical Support Engineers (TSEs) to join the team to help us balance the needs of customers, users and internal stakeholders, while navigating critical technical issues. In this role, you will manage issues from their first symptom to their eventual resolution, communicating with our customers and internal stakeholders throughout the process. People who succeed in this role tend to be empathetic, collaborative, technically minded, and most importantly - customer-centric. They have an interest in learning more about financial services, and are excited to help customers resolve complex issues. TSEs work closely with Plaid’s product and engineering teams, and we have a high technical bar to ensure that we all speak the same language. Our Support team sets aggressive goals to meet the standards our customers expect, and we collaborate cross-functionally with our Engineering, Product, Financial Access, and Go-to-Market teams in order to achieve these goals. This role requires candidates to be based in the Pacific Time Zone (PST/PDT) to align with customer needs and team collaboration

Responsibilities

  • Respond to 10-12 customer tickets per day via Zendesk, meeting quality standards

  • Troubleshoot customer issues using internal tools and documentation and escalate to Engineering or Partnership teams for resolution

  • Work on projects with other TSE’s to improve internal and external processes

  • Contribute to brainstorming and project execution (tooling, documentation, process improvements)

  • Assist GTM teams with customer escalations

  • Collaborate with EPD teams on issue resolution

Qualifications

  • 2+ years of experience in a customer-facing role

  • 6+ months of experience working with REST APIs, SQL, CSS, HTML and a coding language (Javascript or Python)

  • Knowledge of ticketing systems and tools (e.g. Zendesk, Jira), and data visualizations (e.g. Mode) 

  • Preferred: 6+ months of experience supporting technical projects and/or process improvement

  • Genuine interest and passion for Support 

  • Commitment to providing a world-class customer experience

  • Strong written and verbal communication  

  • Self-starter mentality and ability to work independently

  • Effective time management and ability to balance multiple priorities

Plaid’s Executive Assistant (EA) team sits within the People Team and partners closely with the company’s most senior leaders. Our EAs are trusted, strategic partners who help leaders stay focused on their highest-impact work—from managing complex calendars and preparing for critical meetings to coordinating Board logistics, leadership offsites, customer dinners, and company-wide events. We operate as one connected team, sharing best practices, supporting one another, and exploring new technology and AI-enabled approaches to make the way we work faster, smarter, and more effective.

As the EA Team Lead, you’ll lead and develop a team of EAs who support senior leaders across Plaid, while also directly supporting one of our C-Suite executives. You’ll set clear standards, bring consistency and best practices to high-impact areas such as leadership rhythms, onsite planning, and company events, and serve as a trusted partner to executives and People Team leaders. You’ll also help evolve and scale the function through new approaches to technology, AI, and automation.

Responsibilities

  • Lead, coach, and develop a team of EAs through regular 1:1s, candid feedback, goal setting, and career development.

  • Provide direct support for one C-Suite Executive and back up coverage as needed.

  • Set the vision and operating standards for the EA program, including onboarding, role expectations, coverage, and ways of working.

  • Build scalable playbooks, templates, and repeatable approaches for leadership meetings, onsite planning, All Hands, company events, and other high-impact programs.

  • Foster a connected EA community through shared practices, knowledge sharing, and thoughtful coverage across the team.

  • Partner with executives and their EAs to understand priorities, calibrate support, and ensure the right level of coverage.

  • Own hiring for the EA team, including defining the bar, partnering with Recruiting, and onboarding new hires.

  • Identify and implement efficiencies through technology, AI, and automation to improve how the team works.

  • Serve as an escalation point and thought partner for complex, sensitive, or cross-functional situations.

  • Partner with the People Team on programs and initiatives involving executive and leadership support.

Qualifications

  • 8+ years of experience as an EA supporting C-suite executives in complex, fast-paced environments.

  • 3-5 years of experience leading, coaching, or managing EAs or administrative teams.

  • A track record of developing people, with the ability to give clear, direct feedback and help others grow.

  • Experience planning and running complex programs and events, such as leadership onsites, Board meetings, All Hands, and company events.

  • A strategic and operational mindset, with the ability to turn recurring work into scalable, repeatable systems.

  • Strong judgment and discretion when handling confidential and sensitive information.

  • Ability to build trust and influence senior leaders and cross-functional partners without relying on authority.

  • Builder mindset, with comfort using technology, AI, and automation to improve how work gets done.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

  • Comfort operating at a fast pace, navigating shifting priorities, and working flexibly when the needs of the business require it.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
We believe that the way people interact with their finances will drastically improve in the next few years. We’re dedicated to empowering this transformation by building the tools and experiences that thousands of developers use to create their own products. Plaid powers the tools millions of people rely on to live a healthier financial life. We work with thousands of companies like Venmo, SoFi, several of the Fortune 500, and many of the largest banks to make it easy for people to connect their financial accounts to the apps and services they want to use. Plaid’s network covers 12,000 financial institutions across the US, Canada, UK and Europe. Founded in 2013, the company is headquartered in San Francisco with offices in New York, Seattle, Washington D.C., Raleigh, London, and Amsterdam.


Team Overview

The TechOps team is the technical foundation that is a major stakeholder in keeping the company running. We own the systems, tools, and infrastructure that every Plaid employee depends on, from identity and endpoint management to help desk support, office infrastructure, and the internal tooling that powers day-to-day productivity.

What sets us apart from a traditional IT team is how we approach our higher-level goals. We treat corporate infrastructure like an engineering problem: configuration lives in code when possible, endpoint provisioning is automated, access assignment is self-service, and we're always looking for ways to make our systems more reliable and our support burden smaller.

We're a small team with broad ownership and high standards. We work closely with Security, Engineering, and People teams to make sure Plaid's internal environment is secure, scalable, and ready for where the company is going, whether that's a new office, a new compliance requirement, or a new way of working enabled by AI tooling.

Role Overview

In this role, you'll take part in our on-call rotation for a few hours each week, but this isn't just a break/fix IT position. It's a chance to build, improve, and own systems that a thousand-person company depends on.

If you care about doing IT the right way through infrastructure as code, automation-first thinking, and strong security instincts, this team is actively building that culture and needs someone with experience in this area to help us move even faster.


Responsibilities

  • Own and improve Okta configuration, including lifecycle policies, access reviews, MFA enforcement, and Workflows automation

  • Manage endpoint configuration via Iru or Kandji, with a preference for policy-as-code and version-controlled configurations

  • Build and maintain automation that reduces repetitive support burden

  • Evaluate, deploy, and support AI tooling that improves team and company productivity

  • Manage SaaS procurement and renewals for the systems the team owns

  • Actively own and support company-wide SaaS platforms such as Google Workspace, Linear, Slack, and Okta

  • Partner with Engineering, Security, and GTM teams on planned work that crosses into the team's systems or areas of expertise

  • Work from the office 3 days per week


Qualifications

  • 3+ years of experience supporting a large fleet of macOS devices

  • Experience with mobile device management for Apple devices such as Iru, Intune, or Workspace One

  • Experience with configuration as code, such as Terraform

  • Experience with Bash or Python scripting

  • Experience leveraging Claude Code, Codex, or similar tools to improve the quality and efficiency of the solutions you build

  • Experience using and managing major central business and development systems

  • Experience with Google Workspace

  • Experience with Slack

  • Experience with Linear, Jira, or other ticketing platforms

Nice to have:

  • Experience working in a high-growth environment with broad ownership across internal systems

The Workplace Experience (WPE) team is responsible for shaping the employee experience at Plaid, ensuring that our workspaces, events, and cultural touchpoints drive connection, collaboration, productivity, and engagement. Within WPE, the Employee Experience team brings Plaid's culture to life by designing and executing programs that foster belonging and engagement across both in-office and distributed environments, from flagship company-wide gatherings to onboarding, milestone moments, and everyday culture-building. We ensure every Plaid, whether new or tenured, remote or in-office, feels welcomed, valued, and connected.


As an Employee Experience Coordinator, you will help bring Plaid’s culture to life by supporting internal events, employee programs, and everyday moments that help Plaids feel welcomed, connected, and celebrated. You will coordinate event logistics, employee communications, vendor details, and onsite execution for programs ranging from monthly social hours and team gatherings to company-wide events. You will work closely with teammates and cross-functional partners to keep projects organized, respond to employee questions, and ensure each experience runs smoothly from planning through completion. This role is a great fit for someone who is highly organized, eager to learn, comfortable juggling multiple priorities, and excited to provide hands-on support in a fast-paced environment.

Responsibilities

  • Coordinate logistics, vendor relationships, budget tracking, timeline development, space setup, and communications for in-office and remote events.

  • Serve as the first point of contact for employee emails, Slack messages, and support tickets—responding directly or routing inquiries to the appropriate team member.

  • Assist in planning and executing a variety of employee events and programs, including retreats, Plaiderdays, monthly socials, holiday parties, onsites/offsites, and more.

  • Manage operational details and provide hands-on support to ensure programs run smoothly from planning through completion.

  • Research vendors and venues, place catering orders, and create event signage and flyers.

  • Oversee event setup, on-the-ground event management, and breakdown for social hours and flagship gatherings.

  • Provide administrative support for events and programs, including project tracking, note-taking, task management, and swag coordination.

  • Build excitement and keep employees informed by producing event communications such as invites, promotional materials, and recaps.

  • Collaborate with cross-functional partners (People, DEIB, Comms, Workplace Operations) to support broader employee experience initiatives and create memorable experiences for all Plaids.

Qualifications

  • Comfort being a visible presence in the office and engaging employees face-to-face

  • 1–3 years of experience in an events, employee experience, administrative assistant, HR, or workplace experience role.

  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to manage multiple tasks and deadlines at once.

  • Proficient communication skills across multiple channels (email, Slack, decks, event invites, etc.) including clear, warm, and timely written and verbal communication skills.

  • A proactive, can-do attitude and comfort working in a fast-paced, occasionally ambiguous environment.

  • Collaborative mindset and comfort working cross-functionally with different teams and stakeholders.

  • Experience planning and executing events.

  • Comfortable being onsite three days per week in the NYC office(Tuesday–Thursday).

  • Familiarity with tools like Google Workspace, Slack, Canva, Zendesk, or event platforms (e.g.,, Epoch)

  • Experience supporting multi-office or distributed teams.

  • Must be able to lift up to 50 pounds.

Within WPE, the Employee Experience team brings Plaid's culture to life by designing and executing programs that foster belonging and engagement across both in-office and distributed environments, from flagship company-wide gatherings to onboarding, milestone moments, and everyday culture-building. We ensure every Plaid, whether new or tenured, remote or in-office, feels welcomed, valued, and connected.


As an Employee Experience Coordinator, you will help bring Plaid’s culture to life by supporting internal events, employee programs, and everyday moments that help Plaids feel welcomed, connected, and celebrated. You will coordinate event logistics, employee communications, vendor details, and onsite execution for programs ranging from monthly social hours and team gatherings to company-wide events. You will work closely with teammates and cross-functional partners to keep projects organized, respond to employee questions, and ensure each experience runs smoothly from planning through completion. This role is a great fit for someone who is highly organized, eager to learn, comfortable juggling multiple priorities, and excited to provide hands-on support in a fast-paced environment.



Responsibilities

 - Coordinate logistics, vendor relationships, budget tracking, timeline development, space setup, and communications for in-office and remote events.

 - Serve as the first point of contact for employee emails, Slack messages, and support tickets—responding directly or routing inquiries to the appropriate team member.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
We believe that the way people interact with their finances will drastically improve in the next few years. We’re dedicated to empowering this transformation by building the tools and experiences that thousands of developers use to create their own products. Plaid powers the tools millions of people rely on to live a healthier financial life. We work with thousands of companies like Venmo, SoFi, several of the Fortune 500, and many of the largest banks to make it easy for people to connect their financial accounts to the apps and services they want to use. Plaid’s network covers 12,000 financial institutions across the US, Canada, UK and Europe. Founded in 2013, the company is headquartered in San Francisco with offices in New York, Seattle, Washington D.C., Raleigh, London, and Amsterdam.

Plaid’s Data Partnerships team works with financial institutions and fintech partners, and through industry bodies, to build what comes next in open finance across payments, credit, fraud prevention, and personal finance. Our goal is better products and more financial freedom for consumers. We move quickly, with security, safety, consumer control, and trust as the baseline of everything we do.

We believe deep, credible partnerships with financial institutions are what power Plaid’s products and move the industry forward. We fight for consumers, we hold ourselves to a high bar of ownership, and we judge our work by results.

About the role

You’ll own Plaid’s relationships with a portfolio of our largest financial institution partners. You’re their primary strategic and business contact, and you’re accountable for how the relationship goes: the strategy, the execution, the integration, and what it delivers for the institution, for Plaid, and for consumers.

Together with your partners, you’ll influence what consumers experience when they connect their financial lives to the apps they use, and where the industry goes from here. That means building real relationships with people at every level, from engineering teams to executives. You’ll work with Technical Leads to bring new solutions to your institutions and advocate for them inside Plaid, and with Product, Legal, Policy, Go-To-Market, and Engineering to turn what you hear into best-in-class experiences. What you learn from our largest partners feeds back into our roadmap, our policy priorities, and the standards the industry works from.

We want someone who takes ownership personally. If something in your portfolio goes wrong, you’re on it before anyone asks and you stay on it until it’s fixed. You move fast, you catch the small stuff, and when one route is blocked you find another.

You also care what better financial products mean for consumers. Partners should want to bring you their big ideas and their hardest problems, and the people you work with should be glad you’re on their team.

Responsibilities

  • Own each partnership end to end. Lead strategic relationships with several of Plaid’s largest FI partners. Set priorities, get every team involved pulling in the same direction, and answer for the results.

  • Build new products and experiences with partners. Work with institutions on payments, credit, fraud prevention, and personal finance, and support their digital transformation.

  • Earn trust early. Learn what your partners want, what constrains them, and where they’re headed, so they come to you with concerns and ideas as they come up.

  • Know the technology. Understand Plaid’s products well enough to work with product and engineering teams, ours and our partners’, on roadmaps and to make the case for new solutions.

  • Represent Plaid in the industry. Contribute to our policy and regulatory priorities and advocate for a consumer-centered financial system.

  • Be the escalation point. When a business or technical incident hits, you diagnose it, keep everyone informed, and see it through to resolution.

  • Make decisions. Take on the hard calls, make them quickly, and tell everyone who needs to know.

  • Find the next opportunity. Spot ways to grow that fit our FI partnership strategy and company goals, and act on them early.

Qualifications

  • 6-10+ years in partnerships, strategy, business operations, or a similar role

  • Experience managing external relationships on your own and building strategies that help partners succeed with new technology

  • Strong project management and communication skills, including clear executive communications and reports

  • Comfort with technical and product concepts

  • A self-starter with strong troubleshooting instincts, able to reason through complex or escalated problems and guide partners through them

  • Ability to work across teams and levels of seniority, and to influence process so everyone can meet their goals and timelines

  • Composure under pressure and tight deadlines, and a knack for handling the unexpected

Our mission at Plaid is to unlock financial freedom for everyone. To support that mission, we seek to build a diverse team of driven individuals who care deeply about making the financial ecosystem more equitable. We recognize that strong qualifications can come from both prior work experiences and lived experiences. We encourage you to apply to a role even if your experience doesn't fully match the job description. We are always looking for team members that will bring something unique to Plaid!

Plaid is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and values diversity at our company. We do not discriminate based on race, color, national origin, ethnicity, religion or religious belief, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, transgender status, sexual stereotypes, age, military or veteran status, disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics.
